record.paper_title: Lubrication Approximations for Surface Tension Driven Interfaces: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: In a Hele-Shaw cell treated as a two-dimensional incompressible Darcy free-boundary problem whose boundary pressure is controlled by surface tension, can the evolution produce a finite-time topological singularity in which one connected region of fluid pinches off and becomes two disconnected regions?

evidence.quote: For example, can finite time singularities occur, in which a connected region of fluid separates into two disconnected regions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a Hele-Shaw cell modeled as the following two-dimensional incompressible Darcy free-boundary problem. Let Ω(t) ⊂ ℝ² be a bounded, possibly multiply-connected open set occupied by a viscous fluid at time t ≥ 0, with smooth boundary Γ(t) = ∂Ω(t). The fluid pressure p(·,t) : Ω(t) → ℝ satisfies

  Δp = 0 in Ω(t),
  p = σ κ on Γ(t),

where σ > 0 is the surface tension coefficient and κ denotes the (signed) curvature of Γ(t). The interface Γ(t) is transported by the Darcy velocity v = −∇p; equivalently, the normal velocity of Γ(t) is V_n = −∂p/∂n, where n is the outward unit normal.

Question: Does there exist a smooth initial domain Ω(0) which is connected such that the resulting evolution Ω(t) develops, in finite time T < ∞, a topological singularity at which Ω(t) pinches off, i.e. lim_{t↑T} Ω(t) breaks into two (or more) disjoint connected components? Prove or disprove the occurrence of such finite-time topology change for this surface-tension-driven Hele-Shaw flow.
artifact.status_search_result: Numerical and asymptotic studies (Goldstein–Pesci–Shelley and others) strongly support generic finite-time pinch-off in surface-tension-driven Hele-Shaw flow, and rigorous results exist for related lubrication/thin-film reductions showing pinch-off in finite or infinite time. For the full two-dimensional Darcy free-boundary problem with surface tension, however, a rigorous proof that a smooth connected initial fluid region can pinch into disconnected components in finite time does not appear to be available in the literature, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Instabilities and singularities in Hele–Shaw flow
status_evidence.snippet: Pinching singularities occur generically when the system is unstable; an approximate analytical method describes approach to finite-time singularity near bifurcation.
status_evidence.claim: Numerical/asymptotic evidence supports finite-time pinch-off but does not constitute a rigorous proof for the full Darcy model.

status_evidence.title: On singularity formation in a Hele-Shaw model
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous singularity-formation results are obtained for reduced/lubrication Hele-Shaw models.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous pinch-off results are available only in reduced models, not the full two-dimensional surface-tension-driven Darcy problem.

status_evidence.title: Finite-time singularity formation in Hele-Shaw systems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the pinch point where the width of the viscous fluid first goes to zero in Hele-Shaw systems.
status_evidence.claim: Pinch-off phenomena are studied via simulation and asymptotics rather than rigorous proof for the full PDE.
